entities.name: Polemon of Laodicea
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Polemon of Laodicea (144 CE) was a sophist who lived in the 2nd century.

 Born in Laodicea, a city in the Roman province of Asia, Polemon was the son of a wealthy family. He studied rhetoric and philosophy in Athens under prominent figures such as Philodemus and Apollonius of Tyana.

 Polemon's significance lies in his role as a mediator between the Roman Empire and the Eastern Roman provinces, where he served as a diplomat and administrator.

 His work in the field of rhetoric and his writings on the subject have had a lasting impact on the development of literary criticism and aesthetics.

 In his later years, Polemon became a prominent figure in the intellectual circles of Rome, where he engaged in debates with prominent Stoics and Epicureans.

 A striking testament to his intellectual curiosity is his collection of over 200 works of poetry and drama, which he compiled and translated into Greek.

 Despite his influential career, Polemon's life remains somewhat of an enigma, with few records of his personal life and experiences.
